ranges.state: `accept` is the Accept value, or null for a request without it, and `ranges` is the list of its media ranges in order, each with its type and subtype in lower case, its parameters before q as [name, value] pairs with the name in lower case, and its weight in thousandths.

invalid.state: `invalid` is true when the parse refuses the value with the error of an invalid Accept, which the server answers with status 400.

selected.state: `selected` is the type of `types` that the Accept value selects by the weight of its most specific matching range, the first of the highest weight, or null when no type has a weight above 0.

invalid.state: `invalid` is true when the selection refuses the value with the error of an invalid Accept, which the server answers with status 400.

route.state: `route` is the route name of the JSON response.

params.state: `params` is the parameters of the JSON response in their order.

regions.state: `regions` lists the region names of the JSON response in their order.

session.state: `session` false states a request after which the session holds no session token.

actions.state: `actions` is the number of calls of the actions of the application during the request.

handled.state: `handled` is the number of calls of the representation handlers during the request.

storeCalls.state: `storeCalls` lists the calls of the session store that the host passes to the application for the request, empty for a request that opens no session.

parameters.state: `parameters` is the parameter values that the representation handler received, in their order.

selection.state: `selection` is the selection value that the representation handler read from its request.

absentHeaders.state: `absentHeaders` lists header names that the request that the representation handler received does not hold.

excluded.state: `excluded` lists the outputs that the hash leaves out, the `build.json` whose content is `{"build":"<build id>"}` with the build id of `files`.

sortedPaths.state: `sortedPaths` lists the paths of `files` in the order in which the build hashes them.

stream.state: `stream` is the hexadecimal text of the bytes that the build hashes for `files`.

build.state: `build` is the build id of `files`, whose `content` is the UTF-8 text of each file.

context.state: `context` is the JSON text of a context map, which the server decodes and writes again as the same text.

text.state: `text` is the bytes that the hash of `context` under the build id `build` digests.

hash.state: `hash` is the context hash of `context` under the build id `build`.

reorderedHash.state: `reorderedHash` is the context hash of the map that `reorderedText` writes, the members of `context` in another order.

keys.state: `keys` are the keys of the shared data whose keys `shared` lists after the context takes its place in it, or null when it fails.

context.state: `context` is the value at the member `context` of the shared data after the context takes its place in it, or null when it fails.

fails.state: `fails` states whether placing the context fails because the shared data already holds the member `context`.

failure.state: `failure` is a text that the failure of the response, as the response hook receives it, contains.

keys.state: `keys` lists the keys of the JSON response object in their order.

sharedKeys.state: `sharedKeys` lists the keys of the member `shared` of the JSON response in their order.

contextCalls.state: `contextCalls` is the number of calls of the context handler during the request.

firstCalls.state: `firstCalls` lists the first calls of the request in the order in which they run, written `action:<route>`, `context` and `shared`.

selection.state: `selection` lists the selection value that the context handler received, one item for each call.

cookies.state: `header` is text whose characters U+0000 to U+00FF are its bytes, or null for a request without the header, and `cookies` is the map of names to values that its parse gives.

value.state: `value` is the masked value, 128 lowercase hexadecimal digits, that the random bytes `mask` give for the token `token`.

error.state: `error` is the message of the error with which masking the token `token` with `mask` fails.

valid.state: `valid` states whether the form value `value` is a masked value of the token `token`.

error.state: `error` is the message of the error with which verifying the value `value` against the token `token` fails.

hexadecimal.state: `hexadecimal` states whether the masked value of the token `token` is 128 lowercase hexadecimal digits.

distinct.state: `distinct` states whether two masked values of the token `token` differ, because each draws a new mask.

valid.state: `valid` states whether each of the two masked values is a masked value of the token `token`.

fields.state: `fields` lists the values of `text` as `[name, values]` pairs in the order of their names, or is null when `text` fails with HY-42.

names.state: `names` lists the names of the values of `text` in the order of their first occurrence, or is null when `fields` is null.

fields.state: `fields` lists the form values of the body `body` of the type `type`, a text whose characters are its bytes, as `[name, values]` pairs, or is null when the body fails with HY-42.

files.state: `files` lists the files of the body in request order as objects with `name`, `filename`, `contentType` and `content`, where `content` is the text of the file and `contentType` is empty text for a part without a content type, or is null when `fields` is null.

openFails.state: `openFails` true states an application whose open fails with the functions `functions`, written as kinds of `functionKinds`.

openError.state: `openError` is a text that the message of the open error contains.

expected.state: `expected` is the JSON text of the value of `json`.

result.state: `result` is `value` for a text `json` whose value is a value of the data model, `outside` for one whose value is outside it, and `error` for a text that fails to decode.

expected.state: `expected` is the region data `data` after the kept values `kept`, a list of `[path, value]` pairs, apply by HY-38.

selected.state: `selected` is the values of `kept`, a list of `[path, value]` pairs, that conform to the region data `data` and that the server sends in `kept`, by path, each applied before the next.

unchanged.state: `unchanged` states whether the region data `data` is the same after the selection, because the kept values never change `regions`.

reads.state: `reads` is the read paths of the template `template` among the templates `templates`, a tree whose node is true for a path read whole and otherwise holds `keys` or `each`.

kept.state: `kept` is the data `data` with only its read paths `reads` kept.

page.state: `page` names the media type of the `Content-Type` of a page response, `text/html` or `application/vnd.hyper+json`.

handled.state: `handled` is the number of calls of the representation handlers during the request.

session.state: `session` false states a request after which the session holds no session token.

method.state: `method` is the request method that the handler received.

parameters.state: `parameters` is the parameter values that the handler received, in their order.

body.state: `body` is the decoded value of the request body that the handler read.

headers.state: `headers` holds request headers that the handler received.

absentHeaders.state: `absentHeaders` lists header names that the request that the handler received does not hold.

result.state: `result` is the name and the parameters of the route of `routes` that the request path `path` matches, a rest parameter holding the rest of the path, or null when none matches.
`result` is the name and the parameters of the route of `routes` that the request path `path` matches, or null when none matches.
`result` is the name and the parameters of the route that the request path `path` matches after the base path `basePath` is removed, or null when the path has no result.

build.state: `build` is the build id that a `build.json` with the text `text` gives, or null when the file fails; a null `text` is a missing file.

error.state: `error` is `invalid-build` when the file fails with a message that names its path, or null when it gives a build id.

message.state: `message` is a text that the message of the failure of the file contains after its path.

created.state: `created` is the number of factory calls after the uses `uses` of the services whose factories `bound` names.

failed.state: `failed` states whether a use of `uses` failed because no factory is bound for its service.

redirect.state: `redirect` is the location of the redirect to `location`, or null when making it fails; with `notUtf8` true the location ends with one unit that is not UTF-8 text in its host: the byte FF in PHP and the lone surrogate D800 in Node and Python.

status.state: `status` is the status of the redirect, 303, or null when making it fails.

error.state: `error` is the message of the error with which making a redirect to `location` fails, or null.

result.state: `result` is the status of the page with the status `status` and the data `data`, or null when making it fails.

redirect.state: `redirect` is the location of the page, null because a page is no redirect.

error.state: `error` is the message of the error with which making the page fails, or null.

status.state: `status` is the status of the invalid result with the data `data`, 422.

redirect.state: `redirect` is the location of the invalid result, null because it is the route page.

flashValues.state: `flashValues` are the flash values of a redirect that stores each pair of `flashes` in order, a name and the JSON text of its value as a handler of the server returns it, in the order of their names.

changedTopics.state: `changedTopics` are the changed topics of that redirect after it records each list of `topics` in order.

error.state: `error` is the message of the error of the data model with which storing a flash value fails, or null.

message.state: `message` is the message of the stop `kind`; a redirect stop takes the redirect to `redirect` or the page with the status `page`, and `message` is null when making it fails.

error.state: `error` is the message of the error with which making the stop fails, or null.

`error` is the message of the `TypeError` of the method `call` of a redirect, `flash` with the value null under the name or `changed` with the topic, for the JSON text `argument` as a handler gives it, or null when the method takes it.

headers.state: `headers` are the `Set-Cookie` values of a reply after `calls`, each pair of a method of the reply and the JSON texts of its arguments as a handler gives them, in their order, with `Secure` when `secure` is true.

error.state: `error` is the message of the error with which a call of `calls` fails, after which no later call runs, or null when every call returns.

class.state: `class` is `type` for a `TypeError`, `value` for an error of the classes of HY-46.2, or null when every call returns.

value.state: `value` is the `Cache-Control` of a reply after `calls`, or null when no call set it.

error.state: `error` is the message of the error with which a call of `calls` fails, after which no later call runs, or null when every call returns.

class.state: `class` is `type` for a `TypeError`, `value` for an error of the classes of HY-46.2, or null when every call returns.

value.state: `value` is the `Referrer-Policy` of a reply after `calls`, or null when no call set it.

headers.state: `headers` are the headers that the reply gives a page or JSON answer: `Referrer-Policy` with that value, or none.

error.state: `error` is the message of the error with which a call of `calls` fails, after which no later call runs, or null when every call returns.

class.state: `class` is `type` for a `TypeError`, `value` for an error of the classes of HY-46.2, or null when every call returns.

value.state: `value` is the page status of a reply after `calls`, or null when no call set it.

error.state: `error` is the message of the error with which a call of `calls` fails, after which no later call runs, or null when every call returns.

class.state: `class` is `type` for a `TypeError`, `value` for an error of the classes of HY-46.2, or null when every call returns.

notes.state: `notes` are the notes of a reply after `calls`, a list of pairs of a name and its value in the order of the first note of each name.

error.state: `error` is the message of the error with which a call of `calls` fails, after which no later call runs, or null when every call returns.

class.state: `class` is `type` for a `TypeError`, `value` for an error of the classes of HY-46.2, or null when every call returns.

renewals.state: `renewals` are the two answers of taking the renewal of a reply twice after `calls`: whether a renewal was asked since the last time.

embeds.state: `embeds` states whether a reply after `calls` makes the HTML document embed its data.
